title: An explicit counterexample to the six-neighbor square tiling conjecture
summary: Luo, Sun and Wu conjectured that in a locally finite square tiling of the complex plane in which each square intersects exactly six others, all squares have the same size. We construct a counterexample by surrounding a ten-square core with alternating rectangular shells, each formed by six squares. The only point-only contacts occur at the three four-square points in the core; all subsequent contacts have positive length.
